data_fields.name: clip_fps
data_fields.donor_constant: 15 default (ANI_DEFAULT_FRAMERATE); per animation from animfps.2da via GetAnimationFPS

data_fields.name: frame_duration_ms
data_fields.donor_constant: 1000 / fps, integer ms (66 ms at 15 fps)

data_fields.name: release_frame
data_fields.donor_constant: 8 if clip has more than 8 frames, else frameCount / 2

data_fields.name: mirror_orientation_threshold
data_fields.donor_constant: 8 (orientations above 8 mirror the stored clip), listed animation types only

data_fields.name: stance_after_one_shot
data_fields.donor_constant: damage, attack -> ready; die, sleep -> twitch; emerge, get_up, head_turn, pst_start -> awake

data_fields.name: flinch_gate
data_fields.donor_constant: flinch unless immobile, really dead, or killing blow

data_fields.name: resume_pause_gap
data_fields.donor_constant: pause gap added to clip start on resume (no skipped frames)

best_idea: Drive every layer of a character from one master clock, return one-shot clips (flinch, attack, death) to a stance by table when they end, and tie an attack's release to a named frame of its clip.
decision_why: Take the one master clock, the one-shot stance table and the flinch gate; the release frame may only trigger the client's visual cue because Frankendom's kills are server-verified and the client must not decide damage from its clock. Donor gap: the release is an equality test on a clock moved by the draw pass.
acceptance: In the Pit, the strike spark appears on the attack clip's release frame and never before the clip reaches it; a test with a 60 ms render gap asserts the release cue fires exactly once and damage is applied exactly once, from the engine's record.
